clue.text: Legal adviser, very proper, otherwise

parts.note: very means so, as in 'so kind'
licit means lawful or proper
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll miss it'

explanation.surface: A description of a lawyer who is extremely correct, or perhaps quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' looks like it is undoing 'very proper', but it is simply the word OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is the kind of lawyer in Britain who gives clients legal advice directly.

clue.text: Club's bill rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests the bill is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A sports club's invoice has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is a club used to strike the ball in cricket or baseball.

clue.text: A strange team game, recalled layman

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of team are put into an odd new order
recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: An odd sports team brings back an ordinary person who isn't a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like remembering, but it means the game is called back, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone without professional qualifications or expertise in a field.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute or a difficulty to be resolved
a formal word for a person's offspring

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a point of contention and, in legal language, someone's offspring.

clue.text: Ready, my lot: glasses to be thrown

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells their group it's time to start, before the glasses get hurled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning everything is prepared and set to begin, from space launches.

clue.text: Two articles brought in by French priest

indicators.note: brought in by means the articles are placed inside the abbreviation for French

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A French priest has had two items of some kind delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' here means the grammatical words A and THE, not objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Father is the title and form of address for a Catholic priest.

clue.text: Mean boy to become a clergyman

parts.note: par means the average or norm, a mean
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A stingy young man is going to be ordained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for stingy, but it is the noun meaning average.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a member of the clergy, especially a parish priest in the Church of England.

clue.text: Game ends

definitions.meaning: a parlour game where players write parts of a story on folded paper without seeing earlier parts
results or outcomes that follow from actions

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a traditional British party game and also means the results that follow from something.

clue.text: Port in Asian country storing gallons

indicators.note: storing means holding the letter for gallons inside

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia

explanation.surface: A harbour in an Asian nation keeps a supply of fuel by the gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: The port is in Nigeria, not Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is a major seaport and the largest city of Nigeria.

clue.text: Sampler made by vicar and I occupying church bench

indicators.note: occupying means sitting in, so these letters go inside the bench

parts.note: a pew is a bench in a church
Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A vicar and the speaker, sitting in a pew, have made some embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sampler' suggests a piece of needlework, but here it means a foretaste.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a taste or showing in advance, like a sample of what is to come.

clue.text: Still protected by Skye terriers

indicators.note: protected by means the word is held within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Something remains guarded by a breed of Scottish dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean up to now or even so, as in 'not done still'.

clue.text: In an artless way, of course

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both behaving without pretence and, as a reply, certainly or as expected.

clue.text: Playwright from Dawlish: A. Wesker

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of a run across these words

explanation.surface: A dramatist from the Devon town of Dawlish, named as Arnold Wesker.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Wesker was himself a playwright, a decoy; DAWLISH is a seaside town in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, author of Pygmalion.

clue.text: Circular meadow left to be worked

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: worked means manipulated, so the letters of left are rearranged

explanation.surface: A round field has been left to be farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' is a noun here, a printed notice sent round, not an adjective describing the meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a printed notice distributed widely, much like a handout or flyer.

clue.text: Signal made by copper on top of eminence

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the copper's symbol above the next piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A policeman on a hill makes a gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt or sign telling someone, such as an actor, when to act.

clue.text: Nonsense written about hotel party

indicators.note: about means the nonsense word goes round the letter for hotel

parts.note: trash means rubbish or nonsense
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rubbish review of a hotel's party has appeared in print.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrash is informal British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Cause a commotion in lift, one in prison

parts.note: to raise is to lift

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner makes a scene in a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a loud fuss or create trouble, after the biblical Cain.

clue.text: First principle I drummed into singer

indicators.note: drummed into means forced inside, so the letter goes into the singer

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice

explanation.surface: A fundamental rule is hammered into a vocalist's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or underlying principle on which something rests.

clue.text: Fix match in advance

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
down describes money paid up front, as in a down payment

explanation.surface: Rigging a sporting contest before it is played.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests match-fixing; 'Fix' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to secure or fasten firmly, which is to fix.

clue.text: Extremely short, curtailed church service for novelist

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme, outer letters of the word are taken
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: evensong is the Anglican evening church service

explanation.surface: A church service was cut extremely short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives ST, and 'curtailed' drops the G from EVENSONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish author of Treasure Island.

clue.text: About to enter wrong university department

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for about goes inside the word for wrong

parts.note: faulty means wrong or defective
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An academic department is about to make a mistaken admission.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a group of related departments or subjects in a university.

clue.text: Is place in resort memorable?

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sorted again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker wonders whether a spot in a seaside town is worth remembering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town, but read as re-sort it rearranges IS PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something special stands out from the ordinary, so it is worth remembering.

clue.text: Initially pop up with favourite dummy

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A favourite doll suddenly appears at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy, as used by a ventriloquist, is a kind of puppet.

clue.text: Confusing thing, darkness

indicators.note: confusing means mixing up, so the letters of thing are jumbled

explanation.surface: Darkness is a bewildering thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period when the sun is down and it is dark.

clue.text: A street apart

parts.note: way is a street, as in Broadway

explanation.surface: Something is located one road off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at a distance or separated from a place.

clue.text: Sin of English bishop

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing committed by an English churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to do wrong or go astray, just as to err is.
